source.title: Allowed Origins (CORS) is ignored for webhooks with dynamic paths

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
**Bug Description**

For a Webhook node whose path contains dynamic parameters (e.g. `user/:id`), the node's Allowed Origins (CORS) setting is silently ignored. The lookup that resolves the configured origins compares the node's configured path with the concrete request path, and the two can never be equal for a dynamic webhook: a template like `user/:id` registers under `<webhookId>/user/:id`, while the request arrives as `<webhookId>/user/123`. When no node is matched, the CORS handling falls back to reflecting whatever `Origin` the caller sends, so any third-party page can read the webhook's response cross-origin. Static paths enforce the configured list correctly; only dynamic paths are affected. The same lookup problem exists in the test-webhook path, where the registration search also cannot resolve dynamic paths at all.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a workflow with a Webhook node (response mode "When Last Node Finishes").
2. Set the node's path to a dynamic template, e.g. `user/:id`.
3. In the node options, set Allowed Origins (CORS) to a fixed origin, e.g. `https://a.com`.
4. Activate the workflow and call the production URL `/webhook/<webhookId>/user/123` from JavaScript running on a different origin (e.g. `https://b.com`), and read the response.
5. Observe `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://b.com` in the response — the caller's origin is reflected and the browser allows the cross-origin read. The configured `https://a.com` is not applied.
6. For comparison, set the node path to a static value (no `:param`) with the same Allowed Origins: requests from unlisted origins now receive `https://a.com` in the header and the browser blocks the read.

**Expected behavior**

The Allowed Origins list configured on the node applies to dynamic-path webhooks the same way it applies to static paths: requests from an origin in the list get that origin echoed, and requests from any other origin get the first allowed entry in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (which the browser rejects) instead of a reflection of their own origin.

**Debug Info**

```
n8nVersion: 2.49.0 (source build, master @ 75fe21cb)
database: sqlite
n8n_executions_mode: main
consumerId: n/a (local source build)
```

The behavior is server-side logic and is not specific to this environment.

## Environment

**Operating System:** Windows 11 (affects all platforms; the issue is in the webhook handling, not platform-specific)

**n8n Version:** master @ 75fe21cb (2026-11-22), still present on current master (bf31087b)

**Node.js Version:** 24.20.0

**Database:** SQLite (default)

**Execution mode:** main (default)

**Hosting:** self hosted
